title: Stochastic Optimization Foundations
description: Thirty source-grounded questions covering probability, finite-state Markov chains, Markov rewards, dynamic programming, and martingales, with an even easy-to-medium progression.

questions.explanation: An event and its complement partition the sample space, so \(P(A^c)=1-P(A)=1-0.35=0.65\).

questions.prompt: When \(P(B)>0\), which expression defines \(P(A\mid B)\)?
questions.explanation: Conditioning restricts the sample space to \(B\), so the probability assigned to \(A\) is \(P(A\cap B)/P(B)\).

questions.prompt: Which equality defines independence of two events \(A\) and \(B\)?
questions.explanation: Independence means the joint probability factors into the product of the marginal probabilities. Disjoint nonzero-probability events are not independent.

questions.prompt: What does the cumulative distribution function \(F_X(x)\) represent?

choices.text: \(P(X=x)\) for every type of random variable

questions.explanation: By definition, the CDF accumulates probability through \(x\): \(F_X(x)=P(X\le x)\).

questions.prompt: Does \(E[X+Y]=E[X]+E[Y]\) require \(X\) and \(Y\) to be independent?

choices.text: No; linearity of expectation does not require independence.
Yes; otherwise the covariance term must be added.
Yes, unless both variables have mean zero.
No, but only when both variables are discrete.

questions.explanation: Linearity of expectation holds for dependent and independent variables. Covariance appears when expanding variance, not expectation.

questions.prompt: If \(X\sim\operatorname{Exponential}(\lambda)\), what is \(E[X]\)?
questions.explanation: For an exponential waiting time with rate \(\lambda\), the mean is \(1/\lambda\); its variance is \(1/\lambda^2\).

questions.prompt: For a first-order Markov chain, what part of the history is needed to determine the conditional distribution of \(X_n\)?

choices.text: Only the two most recent states

questions.explanation: The Markov property says that, conditioned on \(X_{n-1}\), earlier states add no information about the distribution of \(X_n\).

questions.prompt: Which property must a finite-state Markov transition matrix \(P\) satisfy?

choices.text: Its entries are nonnegative and every row sums to one.

questions.explanation: Each row is the probability distribution over the next state from one current state, so its entries are nonnegative and sum to one.

questions.prompt: Suppose \(P_{ij}=0\), but \(P_{ij}^{(3)}>0\). What follows?

choices.text: State \(j\) is accessible from \(i\), although not in one step.

questions.explanation: Accessibility requires a positive-probability walk of some length. A zero one-step probability does not rule out a positive three-step path.

questions.prompt: When do two Markov-chain states \(i\) and \(j\) communicate?

choices.text: When each state is accessible from the other
When both states have a self-loop
When they have the same stationary probability

questions.explanation: Communication is mutual accessibility: there is a positive-probability walk from \(i\) to \(j\) and another from \(j\) to \(i\).

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes a recurrent state in a finite Markov chain?

choices.text: It is visited at every time step.
After entering it, the chain returns to it with probability one.
It has stationary probability equal to one.

questions.explanation: A recurrent state is returned to with probability one. It need not be absorbing or occupied at every step.

questions.prompt: How is the period \(d(i)\) of a state \(i\) defined?

choices.text: The number of states accessible from \(i\)
The greatest common divisor of return times \(n\) with \(P_{ii}^{(n)}>0\)

questions.explanation: The period is the greatest common divisor of all possible positive-probability return times. A state is aperiodic when this value is one.

questions.prompt: Which conditions define a stationary distribution \(\pi\) for a row-stochastic transition matrix \(P\)?
questions.explanation: A stationary distribution is unchanged by one transition and is a valid probability vector: \(\pi P=\pi\), with nonnegative entries summing to one.
questions.reference: stocastic_optimization/2_finite-state-markov-chains.md — Steady-state and P^n for large n

questions.prompt: For state rewards \(r_j\), what is the expected reward specifically at time \(n\), given \(X_0=i\)?
questions.explanation: At time \(n\), the chain is in state \(j\) with probability \(P_{ij}^{(n)}\); weighting each state reward by that probability gives the expectation. Choice C is cumulative reward.
questions.reference: stocastic_optimization/3_mc_rewards_dp.md — Markov Rewards and Dynamic Programming

questions.prompt: Which conditional-expectation property characterizes an integrable martingale \(\{Z_n\}\)?
questions.explanation: A martingale has zero conditional drift: after conditioning on the available history, the expected next value equals the current value.
Use inclusion-exclusion: \(P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B)=0.5+0.4-0.2=0.7\).

questions.prompt: Suppose \(P(A)=0.10\), \(P(B\mid A)=0.80\), and \(P(B)=0.20\). What is \(P(A\mid B)\)?
questions.explanation: Bayes' rule gives \(P(A\mid B)=P(B\mid A)P(A)/P(B)=0.80\times0.10/0.20=0.40\).

questions.prompt: A uniformly random permutation of \(n\) items is generated. Let \(I_i\) indicate that item \(i\) remains in position \(i\). What is the expected number of fixed points?

choices.text: \(1/n\), because only one position can match
It cannot be found because the indicators are dependent.

questions.explanation: Each position is fixed with probability \(1/n\). Linearity of expectation applies even though the indicators are dependent, so the expected count is \(n\times(1/n)=1\).

questions.prompt: Independent random variables \(X\) and \(Y\) have \(\operatorname{Var}(X)=2\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(Y)=3\). What is \(\operatorname{Var}(2X-Y)\)?
questions.explanation: Independence makes the covariance zero, so \(\operatorname{Var}(2X-Y)=2^2\operatorname{Var}(X)+(-1)^2\operatorname{Var}(Y)=8+3=11\).

questions.prompt: A random variable has mean \(10\) and variance \(4\). What upper bound does Chebyshev's inequality give for \(P(|X-10|\ge4)\)?
questions.explanation: Chebyshev gives \(P(|X-\mu|\ge t)\le\sigma^2/t^2\). Here that is \(4/4^2=1/4\).

questions.prompt: Let \(S_n=\sum_{i=1}^nX_i\), where the \(X_i\) are iid with mean \(\mu\) and finite positive variance \(\sigma^2\). Which quantity converges in distribution to \(\mathcal N(0,1)\)?
questions.explanation: The sum has mean \(n\mu\) and standard deviation \(\sigma\sqrt n\), so the CLT centers and scales it as \((S_n-n\mu)/(\sigma\sqrt n)\).

questions.prompt: For \(P=\begin{bmatrix}0.8&0.2\\0.3&0.7\end{bmatrix}\), what is the two-step probability of moving from state 1 to state 2?
A three-state chain has positive-probability transitions \(1\to2\), \(2\to1\), \(2\to3\), and \(3\to3\), with no others. What are its communicating classes?
questions.explanation: States 1 and 2 can reach each other, so they communicate. State 3 cannot return to either of them, so it forms its own class even though it is accessible from state 2.

questions.prompt: A state can return to itself in \(4\), \(6\), \(10\), and all sufficiently large even numbers of steps, but never in an odd number of steps. What is its period?
questions.explanation: The period is the greatest common divisor of all possible return times. The return times are even and include 4 and 6, whose gcd is 2.

questions.prompt: For \(P=\begin{bmatrix}0.7&0.3\\0.2&0.8\end{bmatrix}\), which stationary distribution satisfies \(\pi P=\pi\)?
questions.explanation: The balance equation gives \(0.3\pi_1=0.2\pi_2\). Together with \(\pi_1+\pi_2=1\), this yields \(\pi=(0.4,0.6)\).
questions.reference: stocastic_optimization/2_finite-state-markov-chains.md — Steady-state and P^n for large n

questions.prompt: A finite ergodic unichain has one ergodic recurrent class and several transient states. What must be true of its stationary distribution?

choices.text: It assigns equal mass to every state.
It assigns zero mass to transient states and positive mass within the recurrent class.
It assigns all mass to the initial state.
It does not exist because transient states are present.

questions.explanation: Transient states are eventually left, so their long-run stationary mass is zero. The stationary probability is supported on the unique recurrent class.
questions.reference: stocastic_optimization/2_mc.md — Steady-state and P^n for large n

questions.prompt: An ergodic unichain has stationary distribution \(\pi=(0.25,0.75)\) and state rewards \(r=(2,6)\). What is its steady-state gain per step?
questions.explanation: The steady-state gain is \(g=\sum_j\pi_jr_j=0.25(2)+0.75(6)=0.5+4.5=5\).
questions.reference: stocastic_optimization/3_mc_rewards_dp.md — Markov Rewards and Dynamic Programming

questions.prompt: State 1 is the target. From state 2, the chain moves to state 1 with probability \(0.25\) and stays in state 2 with probability \(0.75\). What is the expected first-passage time \(v_2\) to state 1?
questions.explanation: First-step analysis gives \(v_2=1+0.75v_2+0.25v_1\) with \(v_1=0\). Thus \(0.25v_2=1\), so \(v_2=4\).

questions.prompt: At state \(i\), action \(a\) gives immediate reward \(1\) and then reaches terminal rewards \(4\) and \(0\) with equal probability. Action \(b\) gives immediate reward \(0\) and reaches terminal reward \(4\) with probability one. For a one-step horizon, which action is optimal and what is its value?
questions.explanation: Action \(a\) has value \(1+0.5(4)+0.5(0)=3\). Action \(b\) has value \(0+1(4)=4\), so \(b\) is optimal.

questions.prompt: If \(\{Z_n\}\) is a martingale and \(h\) is convex with the required expectations finite, what kind of process is \(\{h(Z_n)\}\)?

choices.text: It cannot be classified without independence across time.

questions.explanation: Conditional Jensen gives \(E[h(Z_n)\mid\mathcal F_{n-1}]\ge h(E[Z_n\mid\mathcal F_{n-1}])=h(Z_{n-1})\), which is the submartingale condition.
